headline: High risk: Replit Agent can write/egress from a shared Repl while the paired content-writing agent lacks isolation, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel documented, but B can read/write Repl workspace files and A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress. If A’s outputs are copied into B’s workspace, B may treat file content as trusted. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is pasted into B’s workspace files or prompts, B may ingest attacker-controlled instructions.
IF B parses file contents as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes viable.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Require provenance labels on any file B ingests.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from workspace files.
Use a manual review step before B acts on A’s text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress, so if A receives or forwards copied workspace content, sensitive material can leave the Repl. The shared-workspace risk is enough to treat the default pair as dangerous.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are present in the shared Repl workspace, B can read them.
IF A forwards copied workspace content to external services, sensitive data can be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspace files.
Store secrets only in the dedicated secrets manager.
Restrict outbound network access for both agents.
Separate workspaces per agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP and egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress in a persistent Repl filesystem shared across sessions. A is not runnable and has no write surface, so the conflict is one-sided but still severe because B can overwrite shared files or git state without coordination. Uncertainty about A’s runtime does not reduce B’s default write hazard.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl filesystem, B can overwrite A’s artifacts.
IF git state is shared, B can create conflicting commits or working-tree changes without locks.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Snapshot the workspace before B runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on workspace files and modify git state, so if it consumes A’s generated content as authoritative, errors can propagate into code or deployment changes. A is a content-writing agent, but there is no direct evidence of verification or action-taking by A, so the pathway is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as source material without verification, incorrect content can cascade into edits or commits.
IF A produces unverified facts that B turns into shell or git actions, downstream errors can persist.
mitigations: Require B to verify A’s claims against source files.
Block direct commit or shell actions from unreviewed text.
Add a human approval checkpoint before writes.
Keep A’s outputs in read-only notes.
requires-engineering: implement citation-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration and runs in a Replit-managed cloud environment with broad egress; A is an open-source content-writing agent with broad egress. The pair creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for sensitive data, and the evidence is stronger for B than A, so the compliance risk is driven by B’s handling of regulated material.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or deployment configuration is placed in the Repl, it may be processed in Replit’s cloud environment.
IF organizational policy requires local-only or region-specific handling, the pair can violate it.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the Repl.
Review vendor residency and retention terms before use.
Use synthetic or redacted data for testing.
Keep secrets in the managed secrets store only.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based data routing and retention controls.
